ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in $\triangle ABC$, $AB=CB$, and $\angle ABC=90^\circ$. Point F lies on the extension of side AB, and point E is on side BC, with $AE=CF$. $Rt\triangle ABE \cong Rt\triangle CBF$. If $\angle CAE=25^\circ$, what is the measure of $\angle CFA$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Since $AB=CB$ and $\angle ABC=90^\circ$,

it follows that $\angle BAC=\angle BCA=45^\circ$.

Given $\angle CAE=25^\circ$,

then $\angle BAE=45^\circ-25^\circ=20^\circ$.

Since Rt$\triangle ABE \cong$ Rt$\triangle CBF$,

it implies that $\angle BCF=\angle BAE=20^\circ$,

therefore, $\angle CFA=90^\circ-20^\circ=\boxed{70^\circ}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, point B is on the bottom horizontal line FA, F is to the left of B, and A is to the right of B, so F, B, and A are collinear, and looking from F toward B and A is the same direction. C is directly above B, BC is vertical, AB is horizontal, and a right angle is marked at B. Point E is on segment BC, and AE, CF, and CA are connected in the figure. Reasoning: Since the problem states AB = CB and ∠ABC = 90°, △ABC is an isosceles right triangle, and ∠BAC = ∠BCA = 45°. It is known that ∠CAE = 25°, and in the figure AE lies inside ∠BAC, so ∠BAE = 45° - 25° = 20°. Also, because Rt△ABE ≅ Rt△CBF, according to the correspondence A↔C, B↔B, E↔F, we get ∠BCF = ∠BAE = 20°. In right triangle CBF, ∠CBF = 90°, so ∠CFB = 90° - 20° = 70°. Since F, B, and A are collinear and ray FA and ray FB have the same direction, ∠CFA = ∠CFB = 70°.
